m-01.title: Examine di talk say 'Multiplication always dey make number bigger'
m-01.goal: Understand say few examples no fit guarantee 'always'; make your own cases where di product no big pass di starting number (counterexamples), and explain when e dey bigger.
m-01.material: Minji talk say, 'Multiplication dey make number bigger when you multiply. 3×4=12 big pass 3, 5×2=10 big pass 5, and 7×6=42 big pass 7. So if you multiply any number by any other number, e always go big pass di starting number!'
m-01.thinking.0: Check whether di conclusion generalise too far, even when several examples dey
m-01.thinking.2: Find di conditions wey make di claim true
m-01.prereq.0: Multiplication of natural number and decimal (Grade 5~6 level, example: 8×0.5)
m-01.s.s1.prompt: Which line for Minji story hard to believe? Choose one line.
m-01.s.s1.hint.0: First check say di calculation for each of di three lines correct.
m-01.s.s1.hint.1: Write di multipliers 4, 2, 6 wey Minji use side by side, and look for wetin dem get in common.
m-01.s.s1.line.3: So if you multiply any number by any other number, e always go big pass di starting number.
m-01.s.s1.explain: Wetin you go notice depend on di line wey you choose. If you choose one of di first three lines: dia calculation and comparison correct. Di matter no be 'Di examples correct?' but 'How far few examples fit support wetin we talk?' Na di last line wrong. After only three examples with multipliers of di same kind, like 4, 2, 6, di claim become 'always, no matter di multiplier'. Even plenty examples no fit guarantee 'always' if some kinds of number never enter di test.
m-01.s.s2.prompt: Make two examples with different multipliers wey show say Minji claim wrong. Di starting number must be natural number wey reach 1 or more, and di multiplier must be greater than 0 (natural number or decimal fit work). Di product must no big pass di starting number.
m-01.s.s2.hint.0: Minji test only multipliers 4, 2, 6. Choose one kind of number wey never enter di test, and multiply di starting number by am.
m-01.s.s2.hint.1: Try different multipliers, compare di product with di starting number, and find cases where e no get bigger.
m-01.s.s2.ok.c1: Di starting number na natural number wey reach 1 or more.
m-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Make di starting number natural number wey reach 1 or more.
m-01.s.s2.fail.c2: Make di multiplier greater than 0. (We no include 0 for dis activity)
m-01.s.s2.ok.c3: Di product no big pass di starting number. Minji claim don fail.
m-01.s.s2.fail.c3: Di product big pass di starting number. Compare am with di starting number.
m-01.s.s2.explain: For example, 8×0.5=4 small pass 8, and 6×1=6 equal 6. Both na case where e 'no get bigger'. Even one counterexample fit break 'always'.
m-01.s.s3.prompt: Which statement explain completely and correctly when di product go big pass di starting number, if you multiply di starting number (wey greater than 0) by one number?
m-01.s.s3.hint.0: Change di multiplier to different values and make table of (starting number)×(multiplier).
m-01.s.s3.hint.1: For di table, separate lines where di product big pass di starting number from lines where e no big pass am. Check di difference between dia multipliers.
m-01.s.s3.r.a: If di multiplier greater than 1, e go bigger; if na 1, e stay di same; if e dey between 0 and 1, e go smaller. Dis option state di exact boundary.
m-01.s.s3.o.b: When di multiplier na natural number
m-01.s.s3.r.b: Natural numbers include 1 too. Check wetin happen for 8×1 so you fit correct dis statement.
m-01.s.s3.r.c: Some decimals greater than 1, like 1.5, and some smaller, like 0.5. Di name 'decimal' alone no fit separate di cases.
m-01.s.s3.r.d: If e greater than 2, e must get bigger, but number wey small pass 2, like 1.5, fit make am bigger too. So dis no cover all di cases where e dey bigger.
m-01.s.s3.r.e: Even if di starting number big, multiplying am by 0.5 go reduce am. Na di multiplier decide whether di product go bigger.
m-01.s.s3.explain: If di multiplier greater than 1, e go bigger; if na 1, e stay di same; if e dey between 0 and 1, e go smaller. So di correct talk na 'e go bigger when you multiply by number wey greater than 1', no be 'e always go bigger'.
m-01.s.s4.prompt: Wetin you wan tell Minji? Use di examples (numbers) wey you just make to explain why di claim wrong and when di product dey bigger.
m-01.s.s4.hint.0: You fit use di same numbers from di two examples wey you just make.
m-01.s.s4.hint.1: First talk, 'Minji, dis no work for dis kind of case.' Then add which kind of number you must multiply by to make di product bigger.
m-01.s.s4.selfAssess.0: I compare di product with di starting number clear for my examples?
m-01.s.s4.selfAssess.1: I show say I understand say even one example fit break 'always'?
m-01.s.s4.selfAssess.2: I also explain which kind of number person must multiply by before di product go big pass di starting number?
m-01.s.s4.model.0: No. 8×0.5=4 small pass 8. Di product go big pass di starting number only when di multiplier greater than 1.
m-01.s.s4.model.1: E no always dey bigger. 6×1=6 stay di same, and 10×0.1=1 even get smaller. You must multiply by number wey greater than 1 to make am bigger.
m-01.s.s4.humanReview: Na person wey read am fit know whether di example calculations correct, and whether di learner understand di condition 'number wey greater than 1' or just write am by chance.
m-01.s.s4.check.w1.label: E give clear example with numbers
m-01.s.s4.check.w2.label: E state di conclusion say 'e no always dey bigger'
m-01.s.s4.check.w3.label: E talk say e dey bigger when you multiply by number wey greater than 1
m-01.s.s4.check.w4.label: E no just agree say Minji claim correct
